correctness.rationale: For all integers m>=2 and real gamma in [0,1], detailed balance yields pi_r=u/d and pi_i=p/d, row entropies give the exact formula and continuity at endpoints. The KL comparison shows positive gain only for gamma<e/m and localizes every maximizer to gamma=O(log m/m^2); a uniform O((log m)^4/m) scaled Taylor remainder on this interval and the strong concavity f_m<=-1 yield m^2 gamma*=W(m)+o(1) and the exact scaled gain for any maximizing selection. Separately coded transition-matrix calculations passed 126 combinations; finite tests are not substituted for the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: The selected result is the optimized all-size asymptotic entropy gain and Lambert-W reset scale on cliques, not merely substitution into a general entropy formula. The closest 2022 source derives general transition and stationary laws, but its disjoint-event regular-network optimizer is not the observed-vertex optimizer when reset and ordinary transitions have identical destinations. Full accessible primary text, two related works, targeted research-index queries, web queries, and all 53 recoverable prior own claims were compared. Historical priority remains an independent-review risk.
residual_risks: Published mathematical treatments of entropy-rate optimization under resetting that were not indexed or accessible could cover the all-maximizer asymptotic.
The 2025 density-dependent resetting/complete-graph source was not fully accessible; its search extract does not resolve its relation to path-entropy optimization.
General stationary-entropy formulas precede the theorem and algebraically imply the finite clique formula; only the asymptotic optimized conclusion is asserted as the substantive original result.

value.rationale: On the natural complete-graph test family, optimal fixed-target reset scales as W(m)/m^2 rather than the order-1/m rate suggested by treating reset outcomes as separate observations. The exact maximal benefit decays as (log m)^2/(2m^3). This supplies a structural entropy-accounting explanation plus a quantitatively sharp asymptotic optimization law, not only an elementary normalization correction or a small counterexample.
